definition: Big O notation describes an asymptotic upper bound on how a function grows, ignoring constant factors beyond a sufficiently large input size.
entry_text: Big O notation describes an asymptotic upper bound on how a function grows, ignoring constant factors beyond a sufficiently large input size.
example: An algorithm using a number of comparisons proportional to the square of its input size can be described as O(n²).
label: Big O notation
